title: Why We Have Popcorn at the Movies
paragraphs: Why do we have popcorn at the movies? It might be because movies were invented at about the same time as a new way to make popcorn!
People in the Americas have been making popcorn for more than 6,700 years.

It's cheap and easy to make, and Americans started having lots of it in the 1800s. Then, in 1885, the mobile steam-powered popcorn maker was invented. And soon, people were selling popcorn on America's streets.
Moving pictures were invented at almost the same time, in the early 1890s.

The first moving pictures were small, and could only be seen by one person at a time. But in 1895, the first movie was projected for a large group of people in Paris, France. America's first movie theater opened in New Orleans the next year.
But early movie theaters didn't want popcorn inside — it was too messy!
Things changed after the Great Depression started in 1929. People didn't have much money, so when they wanted to have fun, they would buy cheap things like popcorn and movie tickets.
Popcorn sellers would wait outside movie theaters and sell popcorn to the people going inside. Theaters said this was OK — if the popcorn sellers paid the theater a fee.
People liked having popcorn with their movies. Soon, theaters that didn't have popcorn began to close!
By the 1940s, theaters started selling popcorn inside — and that's where we buy it to enjoy with our movies today.
